title: Per-layer drift detection and calibration runbook for weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) integrations
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Goal: Define and ship a practical runbook and CI harness that detects per-layer numerical drift introduced by weight-only INT8 transforms (GPTQ/AWQ), performs automated calibration passes where safe, and gates rollouts with clear rollback criteria. This ticket covers the integration points with the calibration pipeline, regression suites (nightly and pre-canary), telemetry booleans and alerting thresholds, and an ops playbook for in-field incidents. Scope excludes model training or upstream quantizer algorithm improvements; we focus on detection, automated mitigation, and release controls for serving clusters.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible per-layer divergence metric (Numerical Divergence Score, NDS) implemented and logged per inference request bundle
Nightly CI job that runs a representative 10k prompt suite across a 3x hardware matrix (A100/H100/GPU-X) producing pass/fail and per-layer NDS reports

A calibration flow that: 1) runs lightweight per-layer recalibration for layers exceeding NDS threshold, 2) conditionally marks model variant as ‘soft-fallback’ if calibration cannot bring NDS below threshold
Canary gating rules defined: thresholds, sample sizes, and allowed regression windows (latency and answer-consistency), and an automated rollback policy documented
Telemetry dashboards with NDS heatmaps, per-layer histograms, and a daily digest for regressions; alerting configured for high-severity divergences
Runbook checks and a documented incident response (steps, owners, and run commands) stored in Confluence and referenced from the Canary dashboard
comments: 2026-02-22 – Jordan Lee: Kickoff notes uploaded. Initial outline for NDS metric attached. Decided to keep metric deterministic and seed-based to avoid sampling noise. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/ENG-741852+-+NDS+Proposal

2026-02-27 – Aisha Kapoor: Implemented prototype that computes per-layer L2 and KL between FP32 reference and INT8 activations on a mini-batch. Early results show large deltas in attention output projection for one Llama-derived model; adding outlier handling next.

2026-03-03 – Miguel Santos (review): Reviewed prototype. Suggested adding a normalized clip-to-variance step and grouping layers by functional block (attn/qkv, ff) for aggregated alerts. Also proposed a golden-seed test to rule out nondeterminism.

2026-03-07 – Aisha Kapoor: Added nightly CI job definition and hardware matrix. Draft Canary gating rules pushed: require N>=2000 prompts and NDS mean < 0.02 for pass; per-layer max < 0.08. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1873

2026-03-11 – SRE (note): Benchmarked cal flow overhead: per-model calibration adds ~12% latency to deployment pipeline but is parallelizable. We recommend running calibration in a pre-warm stage and promoting model only after checks pass.
notes: Implementation notes: NDS is computed as a weighted combination of per-layer L2 norm, KL divergence of activation histograms, and a sign-flip detector for quantizer-induced saturation. We store per-layer baseline activation summaries (min, max, mean, var, histogram bucketing) versioned alongside the model artifact.

Calibration strategy: First attempt light per-channel scale recomputation using representative calibration tokens (<=5k tokens) without changing quantization bit-width. If NDS remains above threshold, attempt group-wise outlier clipping and rerun. Final fallback is to mark the model variant with 'soft-fallback' label to route a small percent of traffic to the FP16/FP32 variant until a human review completes.

CI harness: 'nd-runner' binary to run across hardware nodes. Nightly job will upload aggregated artifacts to S3 and create a regression ticket automatically if any model fails the pass criteria for 3 consecutive nights.

Ops playbook excerpt: 1) Identify failing layer from NDS heatmap; 2) Re-run local calibration with larger token set; 3) If still failing, escalate to Quant team to evaluate algorithmic fix; 4) Promote rollback using automated Canary rollback API.
